title: Flatness detected on a complementary open and closed pair
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work either on the small étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], or on the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with $j$ quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaves $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], inverse image $f^*=f^{-1}$ with the canonical constant-ring identifications [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], direct image $i_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and open extension by zero $j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Flat means that tensoring with the sheaf is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every $A_X$-module sheaf $H$,
$$H\text{ is flat}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad j^*H\text{ and }i^*H\text{ are flat}.$$
In particular $j_!L$ is flat for every flat $A_U$-module sheaf $L$, and $i_*M$ is flat for every flat $A_Z$-module sheaf $M$. These assertions concern all ordinary module sheaves, without an étale-origin hypothesis on pro-étale sheaves.

source.place: Tag 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), with the étale sequence in etale-cohomology.tex Tag 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open) and flatness as in sites-modules.tex Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3). Open/closed detection and preservation of flatness are extracted consequences of these sequences and the tensor-compatible exact inverse images, not literal assertions of the localization lemma.
